question.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,6)=\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{6}{{x}^{7}}, & \,x\le -1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=6]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,6)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|6}=-\frac{6}{5}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=6] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,6)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}{x}^{2}\cdot (-\frac{6}{{x}^{7}})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}-\frac{6}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}-6{x}^{-5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{(-6)}{(-4)}\cdot {x}^{-4}]}_{-\infty }^{-1} \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2{x}^{4}}]}_{-\infty }^{-1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=6] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=6]-{\mu }_{X|6}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-{(-\frac{6}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{36}{25} \\  & =\frac{3}{50}.\end{aligned}
$$
